subject: Nanotechnology
title: Quantum Dots for Bioimaging
description: A quick, practical guide to Quantum Dots for Bioimaging.

hook.text: Organic dyes fade after minutes under a microscope — quantum dots glow for hours without dimming.

buildup.text: Quantum dots are semiconductor nanocrystals that emit bright, narrow-band light tunable by size.

discovery.text: Different sizes glow different colors — tag multiple cell proteins simultaneously and see each in a unique hue.

twist.text: Many quantum dots contain cadmium — a toxic heavy metal that limits clinical use in humans.

climax.text: InP and carbon dots are cadmium-free alternatives now reaching the same brightness without the toxicity.

punchline.text: Tune the dot size, pick the color — labels that never fade.

quiz.question: Why are quantum dots better than organic dyes for long imaging sessions?
options: They resist photobleaching and emit brighter, tunable light for hours
They can be seen without a microscope
